notes.content: General Information about the Psychology B.S. degree: The Bachelor of Science in Psychology with an Emphasis in Community Counseling program equips students for roles in mental and behavioral health counseling within diverse and underserved communities. This program prepares students not only for immediate employment in mental health fields but also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in psychology, public health, social work, education, and various medical and nursing programs. Additionally, coursework may fulfill requirements for a range of healthcare certifications and advanced degrees. Approximate time to completion: ~8 semesters Curriculum and Transfer credit information: The program includes 12 units of psychology elective coursework outside of the required program courses (can be transferred) The program includes 20 units of general elective credit (can be transferred) Maximum transfer credit: 60 units

General Information about the Psychology B.S. degree:

  • The Bachelor of Science in Psychology with an Emphasis in Community Counseling program equips students for roles in mental and behavioral health counseling within diverse and underserved communities. This program prepares students not only for immediate employment in mental health fields but also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in psychology, public health, social work, education, and various medical and nursing programs. Additionally, coursework may fulfill requirements for a range of healthcare certifications and advanced degrees.
  • Approximate time to completion: ~8 semesters


Curriculum and Transfer credit information:

  • The program includes 12 units of psychology elective coursework outside of the required program courses (can be transferred)
  • The program includes 20 units of general elective credit (can be transferred)
  • Maximum transfer credit: 60 units

General Information about the Psychology B.S. degree:
The Bachelor of Science in Psychology with an Emphasis in Community Counseling program equips students for roles in mental and behavioral health counseling within diverse and underserved communities. This program prepares students not only for immediate employment in mental health fields but also provides a strong foundation for graduate studies in psychology, public health, social work, education, and various medical and nursing programs. Additionally, coursework may fulfill requirements for a range of healthcare certifications and advanced degrees.
Approximate time to completion: ~8 semesters

Curriculum and Transfer credit information:
The program includes 12 units of psychology elective coursework outside of the required program courses (can be transferred)
The program includes 20 units of general elective credit (can be transferred)
Maximum transfer credit: 60 units
